newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary moves debt to state budget from cen bank.
newsitem.headline: Hungary moves debt to state budget from cen bank.

text.p: Hungary said on Friday that its central state budget will take over a substantial part of the country's foreign debt from the National Bank of Hungary from January 1, 1997.

"The debt (to be taken over) will be some 2,000 billion forints but the amount may change by January 1 due to exchange rate movements," Finance Ministry State Secretary Csaba Laszlo told a news conference.

As a result of the change, which is seen as making the budget more transparent, the central bank's (NBH) net foreign currency position will be zero and the central bank reserves will equal its foreign currency debts, Laszlo said.
The government and the NBH will disclose further details later, he added.
Under the current system, the NBH takes up Hungary's foreign loans in foreign currencies and lends them on to the central state budget in forints.

According to a draft law approved by the government on Thursday which alters the accounting of the country's foreign debt from January 1, the NBH will next year be able to lend limited funds to the state only if the Treasury has temporary liquidity difficulties.
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said on Thursday that the accounting change will result in a larger figure for the overall government deficit.
The figure, including the central state budget and state funds, would be 4.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), rather than three percent under the current accounting method.
Medgyessy said the changes are technical and do not demand any change in economic policy.
The government set an overall budget defcit target for 1996 of four percent target of GDP.
